verdict_rule.statement: A feature is prospective evidence only when its forward correlation clears the declared floor in some period and is not swamped by its correlation with the window that has just closed; a sign change between development and validation, or sign flips in several quarters, is recorded as contradictory rather than as support.

cards.label: Dollar index momentum

candidate_rules.rationale: One-day dollar continuation, the lookback the live F5 already uses.
Weekly dollar continuation, slower than the live one-day threshold.
The counter-hypothesis: weekly dollar mean reversion. Kept so the registry contains the opposite bet.
Position relative to the 20-observation mean.

data_requirements: Daily dollar index values with a declared availability lag (FRED DTWEXBGS is used at two and one business days).
At least 21 usable observations before the cutoff to form the 20-observation window.
missing_inputs: true intraday dollar quotes: the collector reads a daily FRED series, so no same-morning dollar print exists

cards.label: VIX and risk conditions

candidate_rules.rationale: The live F1 regime mapping: high VIX is a dollar haven bid.
Direction of the VIX move rather than its level.
Relative rather than absolute risk level, so the rule travels across volatility regimes.
Credit spreads widening is a stress signal independent of equity volatility.

data_requirements: VIXCLS and BAMLH0A0HYM2 daily closes with a one-business-day lag.
A 252-observation history before each cutoff for the percentile form.
missing_inputs: no option-implied dollar skew and no intraday volatility term structure

cards.label: Relative interest rates

candidate_rules.rationale: Higher US front-end yields raise the dollar's carry; the live F2 threshold is 5bp and is treated as provisional.
The engine's own F3 idea: the spread change is the relative-rate signal, not either leg alone.
German front-end moves read through EUR weakness, which lifts the dollar index.
Long-end US yield change as a lower-weight term-premium proxy.

measurements.label: US minus German 2Y change, five days

data_requirements: DGS2, DGS10 and the German 2Y Schatz series, each with a declared lag.
Consistent quote conventions across the two countries.
missing_inputs: ECB and Fed meeting-date conditioning, and the option-implied policy path

cards.label: Real yields

candidate_rules.rationale: The live F4 idea with a wider provisional threshold.
Slower real-yield trend, so the rule is not a duplicate of the five-day version.
Belly of the real curve, closer to the policy path than the 10Y.
Inflation-compensation change, kept at low weight because its sign is genuinely ambiguous.

measurements.label: 10Y TIPS real yield change, five days
10Y TIPS real yield change, twenty days
5Y TIPS real yield change, five days

data_requirements: DFII10, DFII5 and T10YIE daily closes with a declared lag.
missing_inputs: foreign real yields, so only the US leg of a real-rate differential exists here

cards.label: Fed repricing

candidate_rules.rationale: Dovish repricing (falling 2Y) is expected to weaken the dollar; realised front-end change is the proxy for the priced path.
Monthly policy repricing, less sensitive to single data prints.
The 3M bill trading above the effective rate is the market pricing hikes; below it, cuts.
Repo funding pressure has historically produced a dollar bid; low weight because episodes are rare.

data_requirements: EFFR, SOFR, DGS3MO and DGS2 with a declared lag.
A meeting-by-meeting implied policy path to measure repricing directly rather than through yields.
missing_inputs: fed funds and SOFR futures implied paths are not available from a free source, so every rule here is a yield-based proxy
meeting dates and statement text are absent

cards.label: Economic surprises

candidate_rules.rationale: Needs original-release actual, pre-release consensus and event age. No free vintage or consensus source exists locally, so the rule cannot vote.
Ageing requirement for the surprise input; same missing source.
Release-day conditioning needs a scheduled-calendar source with publication timestamps, which is also missing.
Until consensus vintages exist, this family may inform commentary but must not consume directional budget.

data_requirements: Actual value at first release, the pre-release consensus and the observation's publication timestamp.
An event-age rule applied at the cutoff, not after the fact.
A scheduled calendar of release dates and times in the same timezone convention as the cutoff.
missing_inputs: consensus values and first-release actuals sit behind paid feeds (Finnhub calendar, RapidAPI ForexFactory) that this repository cannot read
ALFRED vintage CSV returns HTTP 404 without an API key, so no vintage reconstruction is possible either
the Fed-bias field is derived from the same paid calendar, so it is left null rather than proxied

cards.label: Cross-asset relationships

candidate_rules.rationale: The live F6 mapping: gold strength is read as dollar weakness.
Equity risk-on is expected to soften the dollar (the live F10 mapping at a longer lookback).
EUR weakness is the dominant weight in the broad dollar index, so it is a confirmation input rather than new information.
Energy strength is treated as a global-growth signal, which is dollar supportive.

data_requirements: Intraday gold history that resolves the 09:30 ET cutoff (local OANDA hourly cache).
Daily equity, FX and energy closes with a declared lag.
missing_inputs: gold comes from a local cache of a previously acquired vendor file rather than a fresh download
the dollar index already contains EUR, so the EURUSD rule is a confirmation input, not independent evidence
